S82.01.note: The settings entry point was not traced beyond the command palette item Settings.
steps: Sign in and click the Settings command: open the command palette and choose Settings, or use the Settings entry in the app menu.
In the settings list, click Billing.
Look at the plan card at the top: it shows Free plan, or the plan name followed by the word plan.
Compare the name with the plan on the Usage page and the account you expect.

S82.02.needs: a paid account (the row shows only when a subscription has a period end)
S82.02.note: On a Free account no period row is expected; this was read from the code, not run.
steps: Open Settings and click Billing.
Look for a row labelled Renews on, Ends on, Current period ends or Trial ends on.
Read the date shown beside that row.
Compare the date with the renewal or end date you expect.
S82.02.where: Settings > Billing (plan card and rows below it)

S82.03.needs: a paid account (a Free account sees only Upgrade for higher capacity)
S82.03.note: The overall meter is the This billing period bar; the Free account shows a waitlist/upgrade card instead.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled Plan usage limits.
Look at the bars: Current session, This week, Most capable models (when shown) and This billing period.
Compare the bar fill and the percent with what you expect from the plan allowance.

S82.04.needs: a paid account (the history card is hidden on Free)
S82.04.note: The flagship cap is the Most capable models bar in Plan usage limits; per-model spend is the By model table.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to the card titled Where your usage went.
Look at the table captioned By model.
Compare the per-model rows with the usage you made in each model.
S82.04.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By model

S82.05.needs: a paid account with some settled usage
S82.05.note: The history shows settled usage only; recent requests appear after they settle.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went and find the table captioned By product area.
Read the rows labelled Chat, AGI Work, Deep Research, AGI Code and Browser.
Compare the amounts with the activity you did in each area.
S82.05.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By product area

S82.06.needs: a paid account with voice use
S82.06.note: The Voice row appears only when the plan has a voice allowance.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled This month and look for the row labelled Voice.
Read the minutes used and any monthly cap text beside it.
Also find the Voice line in Plan usage limits and compare the estimate of minutes left.
S82.06.where: Settings > Usage > This month (row Voice) and Plan usage limits (row Voice)

S82.07.needs: a paid account that has made at least one image request
S82.07.note: The Images row appears only after the account has an image request.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled This month.
Look for the row labelled Images, which shows the image count and credits.
Compare the count with the images you generated.

S82.08.needs: a paid account with a video allowance and some video use
S82.08.note: Whether the Video row always appears was not confirmed from the code path.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled This month.
Look for the row labelled Video, which shows seconds used.
Compare the seconds with the video you generated.

S82.09.needs: a paid account that has run Deep Research
S82.09.note: Research is a product-area row, not a separate chart.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went and open the By product area table.
Find the row labelled Deep Research.
Compare its credits and requests with the Deep Research runs you made.
S82.09.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By product area (row Deep Research)

S82.10.needs: a paid account that has used AGI Code or AGI Work
S82.10.note: Coding and agentic work are split into two product-area rows; the task cost view is a separate item.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went and open the By product area table.
Find the rows labelled AGI Code and AGI Work.
Compare them with the coding and agent work you did.
S82.10.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By product area (rows AGI Code and AGI Work)

S82.11.needs: a file to upload (to see storage move)
S82.11.note: The storage line appears only after the storage numbers load.
steps: Click Library in the sidebar.
Read the line under the Library heading.
It shows the file storage used against the storage limit, or the used amount alone when no limit is known.
Compare the numbers with the files you uploaded.

S82.12.needs: a paid account; a running response helps show a non-zero count
S82.12.note: The row reads active of limit at a time; the counter is only refreshed on reload.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled Plan usage limits.
Look for the row labelled Responses running now.
Start a long response in chat and refresh the Usage page to see the count change.
S82.12.where: Settings > Usage > Plan usage limits (row Responses running now)

S82.13.note: The Credit balances card is hidden for Free and contract-priced accounts.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled Credit balances and read the rows Bonus credits and Purchased credits.
Find the card titled Plan usage limits and read the bars.
Compare the remaining amounts with the balance you expect.
S82.13.where: Settings > Usage > Credit balances and Plan usage limits

S82.14.note: The plan allowance is shown as a plan line and bars, not as its own row.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled Credit balances.
Read the row Purchased credits (bought credits) and the row Bonus credits (promotional or referral credits).
Compare the included monthly allowance in Plan usage limits with these two rows.
S82.14.where: Settings > Usage > Credit balances (rows Purchased credits and Bonus credits)

S82.15.needs: an account that has a promotional or referral credit
S82.15.note: When there is no bonus balance the row shows None with a note about referrals and promotions.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled Credit balances.
Read the row Bonus credits: the amount remaining and the line Next expiry with the date.
Compare the amount and date with the promotional or referral credit you were given.
S82.15.where: Settings > Usage > Credit balances (row Bonus credits)

S82.16.needs: a paid account, and a bonus credit to see an expiry date
S82.16.note: Plan allowance reset and bonus lapse dates appear on their own rows; the purchased balance note is fixed text.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
In Credit balances, read Next expiry under Bonus credits.
Read the note under Purchased credits.
In Plan usage limits, read the Resets in and reset date text on each bar.
S82.16.where: Settings > Usage > Credit balances (Next expiry and Purchased credits don't expire) and the reset lines

S82.17.needs: a paid account with a bar that is not full
S82.17.note: The countdown is refreshed about every minute by the page.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled Plan usage limits.
Read the reset text on a bar, such as Resets in followed by minutes or hours and a date.
Wait a minute and check that the countdown moved.
S82.17.where: Settings > Usage > Plan usage limits (reset text on each bar)

S82.18.needs: a paid account with settled usage
S82.18.note: History is grouped in UTC, as the note under the heading says.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went.
Open the period choice and pick Days, Weeks or Months.
Compare the rows with the period you picked and the UTC note under the heading.
S82.18.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went (Days, Weeks, Months)

S82.19.needs: a paid account with settled usage in a project
S82.19.note: A row with no project name reads Project not in this workspace.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went.
Find the table captioned By project.
Compare each project row with the work you did in that project.
S82.19.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By project

S82.20.needs: an account that has run at least one agent task
S82.20.note: The command palette entry is Work history in apps/web/shared/components/CommandPalette/CommandPalette.tsx; the palette shortcut and any other link to the page were not traced.
steps: Open the command palette and choose Work history.
Pick an agent task from the list.
Look at each row: a cost appears after the time when the run has a cost.
Compare the cost with the Cost and usage section of the task.
S82.20.where: Work history (page title Work history, from the command palette)

S82.22.needs: a paid account (estimate shown for Deep Research); for video, switch to video mode to see the video cost estimate
S82.22.note: Whether the estimate shows before the first step was not verified in the code path; the video estimate is a separate component.
steps: Open a new chat and click the + button in the composer.
Choose Deep Research.
Send a research question and look at the research activity for the text up to ~ with a credit amount.
Compare that estimate with the actual cost in Work history.
S82.22.where: Chat composer > + menu > Deep Research (estimate appears in the research activity)

S82.23.needs: an account with a finished agent task
S82.23.note: On a free trial run the section says the run was metered against the free trial allowance instead of charged.
steps: Open the command palette and choose Work history.
Click a finished task.
Find the section titled Cost and usage.
Read the cost and the token and model call line, and compare with what you expect.
S82.23.where: Work history > open a task > Cost and usage

S82.24.needs: a paid account near a limit (the widget is hidden on Free)
S82.24.note: The composer banner for warnings was not traced to its visible wording; only the sidebar text was confirmed.
steps: Look at the bottom of the sidebar for the thin usage bar.
Hover it to see the title text, for example 80% of token budget used.
Check the bar colour: it changes at 80% and 95%.
Compare the percent with the Usage page bars.
S82.24.where: Sidebar footer usage bar (above the mode pill)

labels.text: Free usage limit reached. Upgrade to continue.

S82.25.needs: an account at a usage or free limit
S82.25.note: The composer banner for plan limits is data-driven; the exact limit text comes from the account response.
steps: Open a chat and send messages until a limit is reached, or use an account already at its limit.
Try to send a new message.
Look at the warning banner above the composer: it names the limit and the reset time.
Check that Notify me when it resets and the Upgrade or Use action are shown.
S82.25.where: Chat composer, the banner above the text box after a limit is reached

S82.26.needs: an account at a limit where another eligible model exists
S82.26.note: The composer action uses the Use name wording from apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx; only Switch to was confirmed as visible text.
steps: Reach the blocked state described in the item above.
Look for a button in the banner or the inline paywall card that names another model, such as Switch to.
Click it and confirm the model in the chat header or composer changes.
Send a message and check that it is answered.
S82.26.where: Chat composer banner at a limit > Switch to (or Use) an eligible model

S82.27.needs: a Free account that can reach a limit, or a limit-state test account
S82.27.note: The countdown button applies to free-capacity cards only; the rolling-window and billing-period limit cards show a reset-time line and "Try later" or "Not now" instead. The plan's old code line 345 is now line 345 for the countdown and 362 for "Try later".
steps: Reach a free-plan capacity limit in chat (or wait for a "No free capacity right now" card).
Look at the card's main button: it reads "Try again" and is disabled with a countdown.
Read the reset sentence under the card text, if one is shown.
Look at the second button "Try later" and the "Upgrade to ..." button, and compare with the Expected: waiting for the reset is offered as an alternative to paying.
S82.27.where: In chat, send a message after a free-plan capacity limit is hit, so the limit card appears. The card's "Try again" button stays disabled with a countdown ("Try again in ...") until the retry time passes. The reset line under the card's text shows when the limit resets.

S82.29.needs: a paid account billed through Stripe, Apple or Google; a Free account sees only the upgrade paths
S82.29.note: The "Buy credits" button on the limit card appears only when the server recovery action is top_up; otherwise the card shows "Upgrade to ..." instead.
steps: Sign in to a paid self-serve account and reach a usage limit in chat (or open Settings > Billing).
In the limit card, look for the "Buy credits" button.
Or open Settings > Billing and find the "Buy credits" section, pick an amount, and read the "Buy $..." button.
Compare with Expected: the user can buy extra usage from where they hit the limit. Stop before paying.
S82.29.where: Chat: at a limit, the limit card shows a "Buy credits" button when the account is a paid self-serve plan billed through Stripe, Apple or Google. Also Settings > Billing > "Buy credits" panel (the "Buy $..." button starts checkout).

S82.30.needs: a paid account billed through Stripe with a saved card (the panel shows "Add a payment method" if no card is on file)
S82.30.note: The panel is shown only when the account can buy top-ups and the billing source is Stripe; the "Billing" tab label comes from packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/settings.json (nav.billing).
steps: Open Settings, then the "Billing" tab.
Scroll to the "Auto-reload" heading.
Turn on the switch next to it (a confirm dialog asks "Turn on auto-reload?").
Set "When my balance falls below" and "Reload with", then press "Save auto-reload" and compare with Expected: you can turn on and configure automatic credit reload.
S82.30.where: Settings > Billing, then scroll to the "Auto-reload" section below the "Buy credits" panel.

S82.31.note: The console group heading above "Usage" was not checked; the sidebar label "Usage" is at WorkspaceConsoleNav.tsx line 132. The workspace owner-only access rule was not verified in the page code.
steps: Sign in as a workspace owner and open the workspace console.
Click "Usage" in the console sidebar.
Find the "Monthly spend limit" block.
Set "Alert at" and the action ("Notify" or "Block"), then press "Set limit" (or "Update limit" if one exists).
Compare with Expected: managed usage stops at the cap for "Block"; "Remove limit" removes the cap after a confirm dialog.
S82.31.where: Workspace console > "Usage" (sidebar item under the workspace console, page title "Usage"), then the "Monthly spend limit" block at the top of the analytics.

S82.32.needs: a paid account with usage history (the Free account QA run showed only paid-plan waitlist text on Usage)
S82.32.note: The "Download CSV" link only renders once the history is shown (the shown && guard); the link points to /api/usage/export with a granularity parameter.
steps: Open Settings, then the "Usage" tab.
Wait until the usage history has loaded.
Click "Download CSV" below the history.
Open the downloaded file and compare with Expected: a usage report file is saved.
S82.32.where: Settings > Usage, then the "Download CSV" link under the usage history.

S82.33.needs: a paid account with usage history (the Free account QA run showed only paid-plan waitlist text on Usage)
S82.33.note: The form uses the period dropdown option "Everything shown" by default; no alternative period label was checked beyond the code.
steps: Open Settings, then the "Usage" tab.
Wait until the usage history has loaded.
Click "Report a billing problem".
Choose the period in the form, optionally add a note, and press "File report".
Compare with Expected: a confirmation reads "Report filed as ..." with the usage record attached.
S82.33.where: Settings > Usage, then the "Report a billing problem" button under the usage history.
